p.title: Prime factorisation of 3825

nodes.info: 3825 ends in 5 and its digits add to 18, so 3 and 5 both divide it.
Divide by the smallest prime that fits: 3.
3 still divides 1275 (digits add to 15).
3 no longer fits, so try the next prime, 5.
17 is prime, so we stop.
Every factor tree of 3825 ends with these same primes — the factorisation is unique (Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic).

p.title: HCF and LCM of 96 and 404

nodes.info: Choose which one to find first. Come back and try the other one too!
Only 2 is common. Take its SMALLEST power: 2² (from 404).
Take the GREATEST power of every prime that appears: 2⁵, 3 and 101.
For two numbers, HCF × LCM = product of the numbers.

p.title: Proof: √3 is irrational

nodes.text: Assume √3 = a/b, with a and b co-prime
nodes.info: Suppose √3 is rational. We can cancel common factors, so a and b have no common factor except 1.
So a² is a multiple of 3.
Key fact: if a prime p divides a², then p divides a.
Now b² is a multiple of 3.
Again, 3 divides b², so 3 divides b.
a and b both have the factor 3, but we said they were co-prime. So our assumption was wrong.

p.challenge: Arrange the steps of the proof by contradiction that √3 is irrational
Ravi takes 12 min and Sonia 18 min to go once round the field. Hop in 12s (Ravi at the start point) and stop at the first time that is also a multiple of 18 — when they meet again.
Draw p(x) = x² − 5x + 6 (set a, b, c). Use the table: which x-values give p(x) = 0? Those are its zeros.
Draw y = −x² + 2x + 3. Which way does the parabola open when a < 0, and where does it meet the x-axis?
a is fixed at 1. Find b and c so the zeros add up to −3 and multiply to 2 (α + β = −b/a, αβ = c/a).
Split the middle term of x² + 7x + 12: find a and b with a + b = 7 and ab = 12. Then the zeros are −a and −b.
Draw y = x² − x − 6. In the table, find where y = 0 and where y changes sign — those x-values are the zeros.
(0, 3), (2, 2) and (6, 0) are all solutions of x + 2y = 6. Make one straight line pass through all three.
Solve x − y + 1 = 0 and 3x + 2y − 12 = 0 graphically. Write each as y = mx + c, draw both lines and read where they cross.
The lines x + y = 5 and 2x − y = 4 make a triangle with the x-axis. Plot its 3 corners: where the lines meet, and where each line cuts the x-axis (y = 0).
x + y = 10 and y = x + 2. Substitute y: x + (x + 2) = 10, so 2x + 2 = 10. Solve it on the scale.
Add 3x + 2y = 11 and 2x − 2y = 4: the y-terms cancel and 5x = 15. Find x on the scale.
p.winText: x = 3. Put it back: 3(3) + 2y = 11, so y = 1.

p.challenge: x + y = 5 and x − y = 1 give x = 3, y = 2. Change only m so that y = mx + 5 passes through (3, 2). What is m?
A garden is 3 m longer than it is broad and its area is 28 m², so x(x + 3) = 28, i.e. x² + 3x − 28 = 0. Drag the corner to find the garden.
Solve x² + 7x + 10 = 0 by factorisation: find a and b with a + b = 7 and ab = 10. The roots are then x = −a and x = −b.
Multiply x − 1/x = 3/2 by 2x to get a quadratic with a = 2. Its roots are 2 and −1/2: find b and c so the curve meets the x-axis there.

p.title: Nature first: 2x² − 6x + 3 = 0

nodes.info: Work out the discriminant first.
When D < 0 the formula has no real square root.
The parabola just touches the x-axis.
D = 12 > 0, so the parabola cuts the x-axis twice.

ΔABC has AB = 3 and AC = 4. Plot Q and R so that ΔPQR ~ ΔABC with every side twice as long (A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R).
p.winText: PQ = 6 and PR = 8: the sides are in the ratio 2 : 1 and the angles match, so ΔPQR ~ ΔABC. BC = 5, so QR = 10.

p.challenge: D is on AB with AD = 3 and DB = 4. Plot E on AC so that DE ∥ BC. By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AE : EC must also be 3 : 4.
p.winText: E(3, 4): DE is parallel to BC and AE : EC = 3 : 4 = AD : DB.

p.challenge: A girl 1.5 m tall casts a 2 m shadow, so the Sun’s rays make tan θ = 1.5 ÷ 2. A pole casts a 12 m shadow at the same time. Slide θ to that angle: how tall is the pole?

p.winText: S(9, 0): the shadow FS is 3 m. Similar triangles: 1.5/4.5 = 3/(3 + 6).

Every point equidistant from A(2, 1) and B(4, 5) satisfies x + 2y = 9. Plot the three such points with x = 1, 3 and 5.
p.winText: (1, 4), (3, 3) and (5, 2) lie on x + 2y = 9, the perpendicular bisector of AB.

p.challenge: Plot the point P that divides AB internally in the ratio 2 : 3. Use P = ((m₁x₂ + m₂x₁)/(m₁ + m₂), (m₁y₂ + m₂y₁)/(m₁ + m₂)).
ABCD is a parallelogram, so its diagonals bisect each other: midpoint of AC = midpoint of BD. Plot the fourth vertex D.
p.winText: Midpoint of AC = (3.5, 3) = midpoint of BD, so D = (2, 4).
